info.title: Custody Core integration API
info.summary: Let an outside platform request, work on, evidence and promote code under the creator's control.
info.description:
Machine callers sign in with a **client assertion**: a short-lived JWT signed with a key registered for their principal (EdDSA or ES256), sent as `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` on every request. Claims: `iss` = `sub` = the principal id, `aud` = `custody-core`, `iat`, `exp` (at most 300 seconds after `iat`), a unique `jti`; header: `alg`, `kid` (the key id). What a caller may do comes from its principal's recorded scopes, never from the token.

Owners use the `/api/v1` routes listed here with their signed-in session (a login with the authenticator code step). Approval and promotion decisions are only ever made there, by a person.

Errors are `{ "error": "<words>", "code": "<stable reason, where there is one>" }`. Nothing in an error contains a secret.

Guides: `docs/INTEGRATION.md` (the whole flow), `docs/WORK_SESSIONS.md`, `docs/WEBHOOKS.md`, `docs/EVENT_HASH_FORMAT.md`.

tags.name: Owner
tags.description: For the project owner, signed in as a person.

get.summary: Who the server says you are (from its own records, never from the token).

post.summary: Ask for a work session. It starts `requested`; a person must approve it.
post.description: Scope `work-sessions:request`. Every text field is scanned for secrets before it is recorded (the record is permanent). At most 25 requests may wait for approval per principal.

202.description: Requested. Nothing can happen until the owner approves.

get.summary: The sessions this principal requested (or, with `work-sessions:approve`, those of the projects it can reach).

post.summary: Close a session this principal requested (idempotent).
post.description: Scope `work-sessions:close-own`. Revokes the session's credential and deletes the gateway's copy. Branches already pushed stay in the repository.

post.summary: Prepare an approved session and get its git credential (or a replacement).
post.description: Scope `repositories:push-session`; only the principal that requested the session. First call (session `approved`): the gateway builds a filtered one-commit view of the repository and issues a credential (201). Later calls (session `active`): a replacement; the old credential stops working at once (200). Failures return the session to `approved` with nothing issued.

201.description: Prepared; the credential is shown once.

get.summary: Which real commit each pushed commit became.

post.summary: Submit a signed statement about one commit of the session.
post.description: Scope `evidence:submit`; only the issuer the request named (anyone else gets 404). Only while the session is running. Sending the identical statement again is harmless (200); a different result for the same `evidence_hash` is a 409.

get.summary: The session's evidence and whether each requirement is met for a commit.

parameters.name: commit
parameters.description: A real commit id the session produced. Default: the newest.

get.summary: Who authored, committed and answers for each commit the session pushed.
Attestations by signing authorities about the session's commits.

parameters.name: commit
parameters.description: A real commit id the session produced. Default: the newest.

post.summary: Deliver a detached signed commit-attribution statement for a commit of your own session (contract commit-attribution-submission/1).
post.description:
Scope `attestations:submit`, and an owner's grant naming this principal, the authority and the project (`/api/v1/attestation-submission-grants`). The scope alone permits nothing.

Only the claim `commit.attribution` is accepted here, and only for a session this principal requested. The owner, sponsor, requester, repository and project are taken from our records: the body cannot name them.

The signature is verified (before anything is stored) with the authority's registered key over the canonical statement described on `AttestationRequest`. Sending the identical statement again (after a lost response) answers 200 with the same receipt and `recorded: false`; a different statement for the same commit is a new attestation, never a replacement.

Errors, all `{ error, code }`: 403 `not_granted`; 404 (not your session); 422 `claim_not_allowed`, `authority_revoked`, `bad_signature` (a changed claim, commit or payload fails here), `unknown_commit`, `issued_before_commit`, `issued_in_future`; 400 `secret_found`; 429 `too_many`; 503 `scanner_unavailable`.

post.summary: Ask for the repository's default branch to be moved to a commit of the session.
post.description: Scope `repositories:promote` (cannot be held with work scopes). Refused (422 `evidence_not_ready`, with the evaluation) unless the evidence is ready for that commit. The request is `pending`; only the owner can approve it.

post.summary: Approve a requested session (only its sponsor).
Reject a requested session.

parameters.description: A real commit id the session produced. Default: the newest.

post.summary: Deliver a signature by one of your signing authorities about a commit. Verified before it is stored.
Ask for a promotion yourself (then decide on it).

get.summary: All promotion requests of the project.

post.summary: Approve a promotion; the gateway carries it out at once (a fast-forward only).
post.description: Only the session's sponsor, as a person. Evidence is checked again. Approving an approved-but-unfinished request resumes it.

post.summary: Reject a pending promotion.
Register the public key of a signer you trust.

public_key.description: An Ed25519 (OKP) or P-256 (EC) public JWK. A private key is refused.

post.summary: Revoke an authority (final).
Let one service principal deliver statements by one of your authorities for one of your projects.
post.description: The principal must already hold `attestations:submit` (a scope can never be added to an existing principal). Revoking the grant, the authority or the principal ends it at once.

post.summary: Revoke a grant (final).

get.summary: Your webhook endpoints, with delivery counts.

post.summary: Register an https address to receive events. The signing secret is shown once.
post.description: The address must be https with a host name, and every address it resolves to must be public (checked now and before every delivery). See `docs/WEBHOOKS.md` for how to verify what you receive.

post.summary: Make a new signing secret (the old one stops being used at once).

200.description: Rotated; the secret is shown once.

post.summary: Stop sending to an endpoint.
Resume sending (its address is checked again).

get.summary: The last 100 deliveries of an endpoint, and what went wrong.

post.summary: What your webhook endpoint receives for each event it subscribed to.
post.description: Signed with `Custody-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>" with your endpoint secret>`. Answer 2xx quickly; anything else (a redirect included) is retried after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 6 hours, then given up. At least once and unordered: de-duplicate on `Custody-Event-Id`, order by `record.seq`. Reject a `t` more than five minutes old.

principalAssertion.description: A client assertion signed with a key registered for the principal (EdDSA or ES256). Claims: iss = sub = principal id, aud = "custody-core", iat, exp (at most 300 s after iat), jti (never reused). Header: alg, kid.

ownerSession.description: The owner's signed-in session (an access token that has passed the authenticator code step).

error.description: In words. Never contains a secret.

code.description: A stable machine-readable reason, where the route has them.

namespace.description: Lowercase reverse-DNS, two or more labels. A label, not an identity.

context.description: Plain JSON, at most 16 KiB, whole numbers only. Never acted on.

id.description: The project owner's id. Must be the owner of the project.

base_commit.description: The commit the session starts from. It must be part of the repository's default branch (checked when the credential is issued).

allowed_read_paths.description: Path patterns the session may read. Nothing is readable unless listed.

allowed_write_paths.description: Empty for read-only access; required for read_and_push.

prohibited_paths.description: Always wins over the allowed lists. A pattern with no "/" matches that name at any depth.

type.description: The kind of evidence, such as "tests" or "review.security".

issuer_principal_id.description: The registered principal (same owner, active, holding evidence:submit) that may issue it.

tied_to_commit.description: If false, evidence about any commit of the session satisfies it.

issuer_is_requester.description: True when the principal that asked for the work is also the one that may vouch for it.

git_url.description: Clone and push here, with any user name and the credential as the password.

token.description: Shown once; only its hash is kept.

payload.description: Optional plain JSON (whole numbers only), kept with the statement; scanned for secrets. Covered by the signature through its hash.

EvidenceSubmission.description: The signature is over the canonical JSON of { format: "custody-core.evidence.v1", work_session_id, evidence_type, subject_commit, status, specification_hash, evidence_hash, payload_sha256, issued_at }.

recorded.description: False when this exact statement was already recorded.

ready.description: Every required requirement is satisfied for this commit.

recorded.description: False when this exact statement was already recorded.

contract.description: The contract and version this server implements: "commit-attribution-submission/1".

statement_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact signed statement. Identical on every retry; compute it yourself to check.

recorded.description: False when this exact statement was already recorded (a retry).

AttestationRequest.description: The signature is by the authority's registered key over the canonical JSON of { format: "custody-core.attestation.v1", authority_id, work_session_id, claim, subject_commit, payload_sha256, issued_at }.

url.description: https, a host name (no IP address), resolving only to public addresses.

events.description: "*", a family such as "promotion.*", or an exact event name.

record.description: What the project's tamper-evident chain holds for this event (docs/EVENT_HASH_FORMAT.md).

BadRequest.description: The request is not valid; the message says what.

Forbidden.description: The credentials lack the scope this needs (or the person is not the one allowed to decide).

NotFound.description: No such thing, or not one you may see (the two look the same on purpose).

Conflict.description: The thing is in a state that does not allow this, or already exists.

Unprocessable.description: Understood, but refused for a stated reason (see `code`).

Unavailable.description: A needed service (database, secret scanner, repository host) is not available. Nothing was recorded.
